subject: The World Around Us
title: Priya's Water Adventure
hook: Where does rain go? Where does it come from?

slides.title: Following a Water Droplet
slides.storyContext: Priya asks Ravi, 'Have you ever wondered where rainwater goes? Let's follow one water droplet on a magical journey!'

points.label: The journey
points.text: Water evaporates, condenses, precipitates, and returns—over and over!

slides.inSimpleWords: Water travels in a never-ending circle!

image.alt: Following a Water Droplet — Water Cycle

slides.title: Evaporation: Water Rises
slides.storyContext: Priya washes clothes in the sun. 'Watch the wet cloth get dry! The sun heats water and turns it invisible. It floats up as vapor!'

points.label: Evaporation
points.text: Sun heats water. Water becomes invisible steam and rises into the air.

slides.inSimpleWords: Sun turns water into invisible steam!

slides.title: Water Evaporates Everywhere
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees puddles on the road after rain. 'Priya, where do the puddles go?' She smiles. 'The sun evaporates them! See how they disappear?'

example.problem: What happens to puddles on a sunny day?
example.solution: The sun heats them and turns the water into invisible vapor that rises into the air.

slides.inSimpleWords: Puddles disappear because sun evaporates water!

slides.title: Condensation: Water Cools
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a cold glass of water on a warm day. 'See these droplets on the outside? Cold air turns vapor back into liquid water!'

points.label: Condensation
points.text: Vapor cools down high in the sky and turns back into tiny water droplets.

slides.inSimpleWords: Cool air turns steam back into water!

slides.title: Clouds Form
slides.storyContext: Ravi looks up at the sky. Priya explains, 'Those clouds are made of millions of tiny water droplets! They formed when vapor cooled high up!'

example.solution: Clouds are millions of tiny water droplets formed when water vapor cools.

slides.inSimpleWords: Clouds are cooled water vapor!

slides.title: Precipitation: Rain Falls
slides.storyContext: Dark clouds gather. 'Now watch!' says Priya. Rain begins to fall! 'The droplets are so heavy they fall as rain. That's precipitation!'

points.label: Precipitation
points.text: When cloud droplets get too heavy, they fall as rain (or snow, or hail).

slides.inSimpleWords: Heavy droplets fall as rain!

slides.title: Rain on Land
slides.storyContext: Rain pours down. Ravi sees it trickling into the ground, filling wells, ponds, and rivers. 'Where does all this water go?'

example.problem: Where does rainwater go after it falls?
example.solution: Some soaks into the ground (groundwater), some flows into rivers and ponds, some is drunk by plants and animals.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rain soaks into ground and fills rivers!

slides.title: Collection: Water Gathers
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a well, a pond, and the river. 'Look! All this water came from rain. It collects here, waiting to be used.'

points.label: Collection
points.text: Rainwater collects in wells, rivers, lakes, and oceans—the water cycle starts again!

slides.inSimpleWords: Water collects in rivers and ponds!

slides.title: The Complete Cycle
slides.storyContext: Priya draws a circle. 'Evaporation → Condensation → Precipitation → Collection → Evaporation again! It never stops!'

points.label: Cycle
points.text: The water cycle is continuous and endless.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water goes round and round forever!

slides.title: Same Water, Always
slides.storyContext: Ravi realizes, 'So the rain that falls today might have been in this well before!' Priya nods. 'Yes! Same water, recycled forever!'

example.problem: Is the water we drink the same water from millions of years ago?
example.solution: Yes! Earth's water is recycled endlessly through the water cycle.

slides.inSimpleWords: Same water gets reused forever!

slides.title: Water Journey Ends
slides.storyContext: That night, Ravi watches the rain. He now knows each droplet's journey—up, into clouds, down as rain, and starting again!

points.label: Summary
points.text: 1. Evaporation: Sun heats water into vapor. 2. Condensation: Vapor cools into droplets. 3. Precipitation: Droplets fall as rain. 4. Collection: Water gathers in rivers/ponds. 5. The cycle repeats forever! 6. All water is recycled.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water cycles through evaporation, clouds, and rain!

subject: The World Around Us
title: Ravi and Priya's Healthy Plate
hook: Which foods make us strong and which make us sick?

slides.title: Mummy's Kitchen Lesson
slides.storyContext: Ravi comes home tired. His mother makes him a meal with rice, beans, vegetables, and fruit. Priya visits and says, 'Your mom is teaching you about healthy eating!'

points.label: The meal
points.text: Different foods give different nutrients to our body.

slides.inSimpleWords: Healthy food gives us energy and strength!

slides.title: Grains for Energy
slides.storyContext: Priya points to rice and bread. 'These are grains. They give your body energy so you can run, play, and study hard!'

points.label: Grains
points.text: Rice, wheat, bread, roti—give energy and strength.

slides.inSimpleWords: Grains give us energy to play!

slides.title: Protein for Growing
slides.storyContext: Priya shows beans, eggs, and paneer. 'These have protein. Protein helps you grow tall and makes your muscles strong!'

example.solution: Protein! Beans, eggs, milk, yogurt, and paneer have lots of protein.

slides.inSimpleWords: Protein helps us grow tall and strong!

slides.title: Vegetables for Vitamins
slides.storyContext: Priya holds green leafy vegetables, orange carrots, red tomatoes. 'Each color gives different vitamins. Green keeps eyes healthy, orange is good for seeing!'

points.label: Vegetables
points.text: Carrots, spinach, tomatoes, peas—full of vitamins and minerals.

slides.inSimpleWords: Colorful veggies keep us healthy!

slides.title: Fruits for Immunity
slides.storyContext: Ravi eats an apple and banana. Priya explains, 'Fruits have vitamins that keep you from getting sick. Eat different colored fruits!'

example.problem: Why should we eat fruits daily?
example.solution: Fruits have vitamins that boost immunity and prevent sickness. Oranges have vitamin C, bananas have potassium.

slides.inSimpleWords: Fruits keep our bodies strong!

slides.title: Dairy for Bones
slides.storyContext: Priya pours milk. 'Milk, yogurt, and paneer have calcium. Calcium makes your bones and teeth strong and healthy!'

points.label: Dairy
points.text: Milk, yogurt, cheese—calcium for strong bones and teeth.

slides.inSimpleWords: Milk makes bones strong!

slides.title: Making a Healthy Plate
slides.storyContext: Priya and Ravi draw a plate. 'Half should be vegetables and fruits. One quarter grains. One quarter protein. Plus milk!' A perfect healthy meal!

points.label: Plate model
points.text: Half: veggies/fruits. Quarter: grains. Quarter: protein. Plus dairy.

slides.inSimpleWords: A healthy plate is colorful and balanced!

image.alt: Making a Healthy Plate — Healthy Food

slides.title: Unhealthy vs Healthy
slides.storyContext: Priya shows two meals. 'This one has candy, chips, soda—lots of sugar. Not good! This one has rice, vegetables, lentils—much better!'

example.solution: Candy has too much sugar and not enough nutrients. Eating too much makes teeth bad and causes sickness.

slides.inSimpleWords: Too much sugar and junk food makes us sick!

slides.title: Water for Hydration
slides.storyContext: Priya fills a glass with water. 'Water is the most important drink! Drink plenty daily to stay healthy. It's better than sugary juices!'

points.label: Water
points.text: Drink 6-8 glasses of water daily. Water is best for health!

slides.inSimpleWords: Water is the healthiest drink!

slides.title: Ravi's Healthy Day
slides.storyContext: Breakfast: oats and milk. Lunch: rice, dal, vegetables. Snack: apple and yogurt. Dinner: roti and paneer. 'This day will keep me strong!' says Ravi.

points.label: Sample day
points.text: Eating healthy at every meal keeps energy high and body strong.

slides.inSimpleWords: Eating healthy all day keeps us strong!

slides.title: Healthy Food Lesson
slides.storyContext: Ravi now understands: every food has a job. Grains for energy, proteins for growth, veggies for health, fruits for immunity, water for life!

points.label: Summary
points.text: 1. Grains = energy. 2. Proteins = growth. 3. Vegetables = vitamins. 4. Fruits = immunity. 5. Dairy = strong bones. 6. Water = hydration. 7. Eat colorful, balanced meals!

slides.inSimpleWords: Eat healthy to grow strong and happy!

subject: English
title: Priya's Mystery Adventure
hook: Help Priya understand stories by asking the right questions

slides.title: Reading Comprehension
slides.storyContext: Priya sits with her grandmother in their village home. The monsoon rain taps on the roof. Daadiji opens an old book of folktales.
slides.inSimpleWords: Learning to understand and enjoy the stories you read.

slides.title: The Mystery of the Lost Parrot
slides.storyContext: One morning, Priya reads a story in her textbook: 'Karan found a colorful parrot sitting on his window. He gave it water and seeds. The next day, the parrot flew away and brought a friend. Now Karan had two parrots.'
slides.inSimpleWords: A story is like a gift—read it slowly, watch what happens, and think about why.

image.alt: The Mystery of the Lost Parrot — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: Who, What, Where, When
slides.storyContext: Daadiji asks Priya questions about the parrot story. Priya learns to spot the main details.

points.label: Who
points.text: The people or animals in the story (Karan and the parrots)

points.label: What
points.text: What happens in the story (a parrot visits, then brings a friend)

points.label: Where
points.text: Where the story takes place (on Karan's window)

points.label: When
points.text: The time of the story (morning, then next day)

slides.inSimpleWords: Always ask these 4 questions to understand any story.

image.alt: Who, What, Where, When — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: The Main Idea
slides.storyContext: Sunny barks at a lizard on the wall. Priya thinks: 'This is a small detail. The BIG idea in the parrot story is: kindness brings friendship.'

points.text: A story has a main idea—the most important thing that happens
Small details support the main idea (Karan gave water and seeds)
The main idea teaches us something (be kind to animals)

slides.inSimpleWords: The main idea is like the heart of the story; everything else supports it.

slides.title: Finding the Order of Events
slides.storyContext: Priya uses three stones to mark: First stone (Karan finds parrot), middle stone (he gives food), last stone (parrot brings a friend). This is the order things happen.

points.text: Events happen in order: first, then, finally
Words like 'morning', 'next day', 'then' show order
Knowing the order helps you understand the story better

slides.inSimpleWords: Stories move forward like steps up a ladder—one thing after another.

image.alt: Finding the Order of Events — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: Understanding Feelings
slides.storyContext: Priya asks: 'How did Karan feel when the parrot came back with a friend?' Daadiji smiles: 'His heart was full of joy! He loved the animals even more.'

points.text: Characters have feelings (happy, sad, scared, excited)
We know their feelings from what they DO (Karan gave food = he cares)
Understanding feelings helps us like the story more

slides.inSimpleWords: Good readers feel what the characters feel.

slides.title: Read and Answer
slides.storyContext: Daadiji gives Priya a short story to practice: 'Meera went to the market with her mother. She saw a stall with colorful ribbons. She chose a blue ribbon for her sister's hair. Her sister danced with joy.'

example.problem: Read the story and tell: (1) Who is the main person? (2) What did Meera do? (3) Where did it happen? (4) How did Meera's sister feel?
example.solution: (1) Meera. (2) She went to the market and bought a blue ribbon. (3) At the market. (4) Happy and joyful—she danced!

slides.inSimpleWords: Always ask WHO, WHAT, WHERE, WHEN to answer questions about stories.

slides.title: Your Turn: Mini Story
slides.storyContext: Priya's teacher gives her a short passage: 'Ram liked to play cricket. One day, he broke the ball. He felt sad. But his friend Asha gave him a new ball. Ram was very happy. They played together until sunset.'

example.problem: Answer: (1) What was the problem? (2) How was it solved? (3) What is the main idea?
example.solution: (1) Ram broke his ball. (2) Asha gave him a new ball. (3) Real friends help when we are sad.

slides.inSimpleWords: Read carefully, ask questions, and think about what the story teaches.

image.alt: Your Turn: Mini Story — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: How to Understand Stories

points.text: Ask WHO, WHAT, WHERE, WHEN to find key details
Find the main idea—what the story is really about
Notice the order of events (first, then, finally)
Understand how characters feel
Good readers ask questions and think deeply

slides.inSimpleWords: Reading is like detective work—look for clues and understand the whole picture!

image.alt: How to Understand Stories — Reading Comprehension
